VIDEO.title: Matthew 12:38-50 – Why Jesus Said Seven Worse Spirits Could Come Back!
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

hand: Behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 12:38-50. Scribes and Pharisees ask for a sign, after miracles they could not deny. Jesus refuses and gives only the sign of Jonah, pointing to His death and resurrection. The men of Nineveh and the Queen of the South will condemn this generation, for 'something greater' is here. Then He speaks of an unclean spirit that returns with seven worse, and says His family are those who do the Father's will.

Signs in the Old Testament were God's gracious gift, but not something to demand out of unbelief. When Yahweh offered Ahaz a sign, he refused to ask (Isaiah 7:10-12). The demand for a sign parallels the devil's 'If You are the Son of God' in Matthew 4.

Jesus says 'something greater,' not 'someone,' as in 12:6: He includes Himself and all His works for God's kingdom. The judgment He mentions is the day of Yahweh (Isaiah 2:12-17; Daniel 7:9-10). Nineveh, Israel's proud enemy, repented at lesser preaching; the Queen of Sheba came with hard questions and blessed Yahweh.

Unclean spirits in waterless places: Isaiah 13, Isaiah 34 and Jeremiah 50 picture ruins overrun by desert creatures, among them the 'night creature' (lilith). Following Michael Heiser, the video reads these as literary pictures of evil spirits; in Second Temple Judaism the wilderness was where evil spirits dwelt, a kind of anti-Eden.

The key word is 'house.' In Hebrew bayit also means temple (Bethel, 'house of God'). Jesus likely pointed at the healed man nearby: as a spirit returns with seven worse to an empty house, so it will be with the house of Israel, which had no room for the Spirit of God. Compare 'your house is being left to you desolate' (23:38).

The lesson for the original audience: God is unwilling to reveal His activity to those who are unwilling to recognize it. For us: stay humble, trusting and dependent, like little children (11:25-26), so we keep recognizing God's activity around us.
QUOTES: God is unwilling to reveal his activity to those who are unwilling to recognize it.
Signs were given in the Old Testament as a gracious gift of God.
The wilderness is basically the anti-Eden.
God's activity does not stop at the point of our salvation.

LSB_QUOTES.text: for just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
Ask a sign for yourself from Yahweh your God; make it deep as Sheol or high as heaven.
For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, he is My brother and sister and mother.

src.text: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered and said to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.” But He answered and said to them, “An evil and adulterous generation eagerly seeks for a sign; and yet no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet;

lines.text: This comes after miracles even they could not deny, so it is not a genuine request; it shows willful ignorance. They likely wanted something that fit their own expectations.
'Adulterous' is the prophets' word for unfaithful Israel (Ezekiel 16:32). The demand also echoes the devil's 'If You are the Son of God' (4:3, 6).

src.text: “Ask a sign for yourself from Yahweh your God; make it deep as Sheol or high as heaven.” But Ahaz said, “I will not ask, and I will not test Yahweh!”

lines.text: Did God give signs in the Old Testament? Absolutely, as a gracious gift. But they were not given because people demanded more evidence for their unbelief.

Isaiah does not praise Ahaz's answer: 'Is it too slight a thing for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my God as well?' (Isaiah 7:13). Then he announces the sign of Immanuel (Isaiah 7:14).

left.text: And Yahweh appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the stomach of the fish three days and three nights.

right.text: The men of Nineveh will stand up with this generation at the judgment, and will condemn it because they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.

lines.text: Jonah's three days point to Jesus' death and resurrection. But the Ninevites, Assyrians, were proud, longtime enemies of God's people; in 701 BC Assyria nearly took Jerusalem. The Pharisees are like them in pride, and unlike them because Nineveh repented.
'The judgment' is shorthand for the day of Yahweh (Ezekiel 13:5; Isaiah 2:12-17), when, in Daniel's vision, 'the court sat, and the books were opened' (Daniel 7:10).

src.text: Blessed be Yahweh your God who delighted in you, to set you on the throne of Israel; because Yahweh loved Israel forever, therefore He made you king, to do justice and righteousness.”

lines.text: The queen of Sheba came to test Solomon with hard questions (the LSB says 'riddles') because at first she did not believe the reports. The Pharisees are like her, questioning; but unlike her, they will not bless God for the One He has set over Israel.
'Something greater,' not 'someone greater': as in 12:6, Jesus includes Himself and the whole of His work for God's kingdom.

src.text: “Now when the unclean spirit goes out of a man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came’; and when it comes, it finds it unoccupied, swept, and put in order. Then it goes and takes along with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and live there; and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. That is the way it will also be with this evil generation.”

lines.text: It sounds like a change of subject, but it is all connected. In Second Temple Judaism the wilderness was a place where evil spirits dwelt: a symbol of chaos, exile and separation from God's presence, an anti-Eden. Following Michael Heiser, the video adds that the barren desert was a picture of the realm of the dead.
On the Day of Atonement the goat for Azazel was sent 'into the wilderness' (Leviticus 16:10).

src.text: And the desert creatures will meet with the wolves; / The hairy goat also will cry to its kind; / Surely, the night creature will obtain relief there / And will find itself a resting place.

lines.text: Jesus likely drew the picture partly from Isaiah 13:20-21, Isaiah 34:14 and Jeremiah 50:39, where the ruins of Babylon and Edom are overrun by desert creatures.

The Hebrew uses words tied to illegitimate sacrifices ('hairy goat,' se'irim) and lilith, 'night creature,' which later Jewish thought made a night demon. Heiser and others read these creatures as literary pictures of evil spirits, not literal animals.
Notice that the night creature finds 'a resting place' in the ruins, while Jesus' unclean spirit seeks rest and does not find it.

left.text: Behold, your house is being left to you desolate!

right.text: And He answered and said to them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I say to you, not one stone here will be left upon another, which will not be torn down.”

lines.text: Why call a person a house? In Hebrew, bayit is house and also temple: Bethel means 'house of God.' Like a good rabbi, Jesus is likely pointing at the healed man still standing nearby.

As the spirit returns with seven worse, so it will be with the house of Israel. If there is no place for the Spirit of God in the house, it will be overrun by evil. Jesus says it again in 23:37-38 and 24:2.

src.text: But Jesus answered the one who was telling Him and said, “Who is My mother and who are My brothers?” And stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He said, “Behold My mother and My brothers! For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, he is My brother and sister and mother.”

lines.text: His mother and brothers seek to speak to Him while He is still speaking: they interrupt His teaching. Some suggest they were at odds with what He said, or with Him, or both.
If so, opposition was coming from all sides: crowds, leaders and family. His family are those who do the Father's will.
Mark says His own people came 'to take custody of Him; for they were saying, “He has lost His senses”' (Mark 3:21), and John: 'not even His brothers were believing in Him' (John 7:5).
Remember Jesus' prayer: hidden from the wise, revealed to infants (11:25-26). Humility, trust and dependence are the key to God revealing His will.
At salvation we cried out to God in humility and dependence. That is only the beginning; God keeps working, and we stay in that posture so we keep recognizing His activity around us.

TERMS.def: A miraculous token that confirms God's word; in the Old Testament a gracious gift, not something to demand.
The prophets' picture of unfaithful Israel as an adulteress (Ezekiel 16:32).
The day of the Lord's judgment against the proud (Isaiah 2:12-17); 'the judgment' in 12:41-42.
The queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10), from the far south of Arabia.
Desert wilderness, thought to be a haunt of evil spirits.
Hebrew lilith, 'night creature' (Isaiah 34:14); later Jewish legend made it a female night demon. The captions write 'liit.'
Jewish life and thought from the return from exile (about 516 BC) to the temple's fall in AD 70.
Hebrew 'house'; also household, dynasty, and temple ('house of Yahweh'). The captions write 'bait.'

WORDS.gloss: Adulteress; as an adjective, adulterous, unfaithful to God.
Comparative of polys (much): more, greater; here neuter, 'something greater.' The LSB tags it under polys. Look up: BDAG, πλείων.
To be unoccupied, empty; to have leisure.
Night creature; later legend, a night demon. Look up: BDB or HALOT, לִילִית.
House, household; temple. Look up: BDB or HALOT, בַּיִת.

BACKGROUND.p: Nineveh was a capital of the Assyrian empire, which destroyed Samaria in 722 BC. In 701 BC Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem but did not take it (2 Kings 18-19). Nineveh itself fell in 612 BC.
Sheba was a kingdom of southern Arabia (probably in today's Yemen), rich from the incense trade. For Jesus' hearers she came 'from the ends of the earth' (12:42).
Jews often counted any part of a day as a day, so Friday afternoon to Sunday morning could be spoken of as three days (compare Esther 4:16 with 5:1).

Second Temple writings often place evil spirits in desolate places; in Tobit a demon flees to the far parts of Egypt (Tobit 8:3). The Day of Atonement goat was sent away 'to Azazel' in the wilderness (Leviticus 16:8-10).

WITNESSES.text: Could then anything be more foolish than these men (not more impious only), who after so many miracles, as though none had been wrought, say, We would see a sign from You?

WITNESSES.text: Let them hear that a considerate mind is needed, and if this be wanting, signs are of no profit.

WITNESSES.text: For this makes one His mother much more, than those pangs did.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 44, on 12:50. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

DEBATES.p: The video: a double meaning, the healed man and the house of Israel (bayit as temple), pointing ahead to 23:38. Most commentators agree the parable is about 'this evil generation' (12:45); fewer press the temple sense.
Matthew does not say why they came. Mark 3:21 suggests they thought He was out of His mind; Catholic and Orthodox readers often stress Mary's faithfulness and read 'brothers' as relatives.
Some read Isaiah 34's creatures as ordinary wild animals of a ruin; others, with Heiser, as demonic figures. Ancient translations differ (the Septuagint has 'onocentaurs').

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The video says Ahaz 'responds appropriately' when he will not ask for a sign. Isaiah answers him with a rebuke: 'Is it too slight a thing for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my God as well?' (Isaiah 7:13). Ahaz's pious-sounding refusal hid his unbelief.
The day of Yahweh text is Isaiah 2:12 (the video says 'Isaiah 6:12').
Nahum 3 condemns Nineveh's bloodshed and harlotries; its pride is clearest in Zephaniah 2:15: 'I am, and there is no one besides me.'
Jesus does not refuse to see His mother and brothers in the text; He answers the messenger and points to His disciples.
The claims credited to Michael Heiser about the wilderness and the desert creatures are summaries we could not check against his books.
The captions write 'Jonah 1:1 17' for Jonah 1:17, 'liit' for lilith, 'bait' for bayit, and 'BL' for Bethel.

QUESTIONS: Have you ever asked God for a sign when He had already shown you enough? What was underneath the request?
How are the Pharisees like the Ninevites and the queen of Sheba, and how are they unlike them?
What does it mean for a heart to be 'swept and put in order' but empty? How is that dangerous?
What fills your 'house' when something bad is cleared out of it?
Who are your brothers and sisters by Jesus' definition in 12:50?
Where might you be unwilling to recognize God's activity right now?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson for the original audience: God is unwilling to reveal His activity to those who are unwilling to recognize it. The scribes and Pharisees refused to recognize Jesus as Lord and Savior, and because of their personal vendetta they blinded themselves to the true explanation for the miracles they saw. This cuts deep, and it is not only for those outside the church. Remember Jesus' prayer: hidden from the wise, revealed to little children (11:25-26). Humility, trust and dependence are the key to God revealing His will. At our salvation we cried out to God in humility, recognizing our sin and our need. That is only the beginning: God's activity does not stop at the point of our salvation, and we are invited to take part in His continuing work. So we must stay in that posture, humble, trusting and dependent on the Lord at all times, so that we keep recognizing His activity all around us.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): read Jonah 3 and 1 Kings 10:1-9 this week. Each evening, write one way you saw God at work that day, and one place you were tempted to demand more proof before obeying.

## The spirit and the empty house
1. Matthew 12:43: Waterless places
   Wilderness Matthew 12:43-45: "“Now when the unclean spirit goes out of a man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came’; and when it comes, it finds it unoccupied, swept, and put in order. Then it goes and takes along with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and live there; and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. That is the way it will also be with this evil generation.”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+12:43-45
   (video) It sounds like a change of subject, but it is all connected. In Second Temple Judaism the wilderness was a place where evil spirits dwelt: a symbol of chaos, exile and separation from God's presence, an anti-Eden. Following Michael Heiser, the video adds that the barren desert was a picture of the realm of the dead.
   [Background] On the Day of Atonement the goat for Azazel was sent 'into the wilderness' (Leviticus 16:10). (Leviticus 16:10)
2. Isaiah 13 and 34; Jeremiah 50: The night creature
   Lilith Isaiah 34:14: "And the desert creatures will meet with the wolves; / The hairy goat also will cry to its kind; / Surely, the night creature will obtain relief there / And will find itself a resting place." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Isaiah+34:14
   (video) Jesus likely drew the picture partly from Isaiah 13:20-21, Isaiah 34:14 and Jeremiah 50:39, where the ruins of Babylon and Edom are overrun by desert creatures. (Isaiah 13:20-21; Jeremiah 50:39)
   (video) The Hebrew uses words tied to illegitimate sacrifices ('hairy goat,' se'irim) and lilith, 'night creature,' which later Jewish thought made a night demon. Heiser and others read these creatures as literary pictures of evil spirits, not literal animals.
   [Background] Notice that the night creature finds 'a resting place' in the ruins, while Jesus' unclean spirit seeks rest and does not find it.
3. Matthew 12:44-45: The empty house
   Jesus (Matthew 23:38, LSB): "Behold, your house is being left to you desolate!"
   Jesus (Matthew 24:2, LSB): "And He answered and said to them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I say to you, not one stone here will be left upon another, which will not be torn down.”"
   (video) Why call a person a house? In Hebrew, bayit is house and also temple: Bethel means 'house of God.' Like a good rabbi, Jesus is likely pointing at the healed man still standing nearby.
   (video) As the spirit returns with seven worse, so it will be with the house of Israel. If there is no place for the Spirit of God in the house, it will be overrun by evil. Jesus says it again in 23:37-38 and 24:2. (Matthew 23:37-38)

## Jesus' true family
1. Matthew 12:46-50: Who is My mother?
   Family Matthew 12:48-50: "But Jesus answered the one who was telling Him and said, “Who is My mother and who are My brothers?” And stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He said, “Behold My mother and My brothers! For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, he is My brother and sister and mother.”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+12:48-50
   (video) His mother and brothers seek to speak to Him while He is still speaking: they interrupt His teaching. Some suggest they were at odds with what He said, or with Him, or both.
   (video) If so, opposition was coming from all sides: crowds, leaders and family. His family are those who do the Father's will.
   [Background] Mark says His own people came 'to take custody of Him; for they were saying, “He has lost His senses”' (Mark 3:21), and John: 'not even His brothers were believing in Him' (John 7:5). (Mark 3:21; John 7:5)
2. Matthew 11:25-26: Stay like little children
   (video) Remember Jesus' prayer: hidden from the wise, revealed to infants (11:25-26). Humility, trust and dependence are the key to God revealing His will. (Matthew 11:25-26)
   (video) At salvation we cried out to God in humility and dependence. That is only the beginning; God keeps working, and we stay in that posture so we keep recognizing His activity around us.

## Key people
- Jesus: Refuses a sign on demand and points to Jonah; 'something greater' is here. [Background] Luke says Jonah 'became a sign to the Ninevites' (Luke 11:30).
- The scribes and Pharisees: Demand a sign after miracles they could not deny: willful ignorance. [Background] They ask again in 16:1-4 and get the same answer.
- Jonah: Three days and three nights in the fish; his preaching brought Nineveh to repent. [Background] A prophet from Gath-hepher in Galilee (2 Kings 14:25).
- The men of Nineveh: Proud Assyrians, enemies of God's people, who still repented. [Background] Nahum later announced Nineveh's fall (Nahum 3:1-7).
- The Queen of the South: Came with hard questions, saw Solomon's wisdom and blessed Yahweh. [Background] She said, 'I did not believe those words, until I came and my eyes had seen it' (1 Kings 10:7).
- Jesus' mother and brothers: Stand outside seeking to speak to Him, interrupting His teaching. [Background] After the resurrection His mother and brothers are with the disciples in prayer (Acts 1:14).

## Places [Background]
- Joppa: Where Jonah boarded a ship to flee from Yahweh (Jonah 1:3).
- Gath-hepher: Jonah's home town in Galilee (2 Kings 14:25), a few miles from Nazareth.
- Capernaum: Jesus' base in Galilee, where much of chapter 12 likely took place.
- Bethel (named in the video): Its name means house of God (Genesis 28:19): the video's example that bayit, house, can mean temple.
- Jerusalem (named in the video): Solomon's city and temple; Assyria nearly took it in 701 BC. 'Your house is being left to you desolate' (23:38).

## Key terms
- Sign: A miraculous token that confirms God's word; in the Old Testament a gracious gift, not something to demand.
- Adulterous generation: The prophets' picture of unfaithful Israel as an adulteress (Ezekiel 16:32).
- Day of Yahweh: The day of the Lord's judgment against the proud (Isaiah 2:12-17); 'the judgment' in 12:41-42.
- Queen of the South: The queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10), from the far south of Arabia.
- Waterless places: Desert wilderness, thought to be a haunt of evil spirits.
- Lilith: Hebrew lilith, 'night creature' (Isaiah 34:14); later Jewish legend made it a female night demon. The captions write 'liit.'
- Second Temple Judaism: Jewish life and thought from the return from exile (about 516 BC) to the temple's fall in AD 70.
- Bayit: Hebrew 'house'; also household, dynasty, and temple ('house of Yahweh'). The captions write 'bait.'

- οἶκος oikos (G3624, Greek): House, household; also the temple. (Matt 12:44; 23:38)

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Nineveh and Assyria: Nineveh was a capital of the Assyrian empire, which destroyed Samaria in 722 BC. In 701 BC Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem but did not take it (2 Kings 18-19). Nineveh itself fell in 612 BC.
- Sheba: Sheba was a kingdom of southern Arabia (probably in today's Yemen), rich from the incense trade. For Jesus' hearers she came 'from the ends of the earth' (12:42).
- Three days and three nights: Jews often counted any part of a day as a day, so Friday afternoon to Sunday morning could be spoken of as three days (compare Esther 4:16 with 5:1).
- Spirits in the wilderness: Second Temple writings often place evil spirits in desolate places; in Tobit a demon flees to the far parts of Egypt (Tobit 8:3). The Day of Atonement goat was sent away 'to Azazel' in the wilderness (Leviticus 16:8-10).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Who is the house? The video: a double meaning, the healed man and the house of Israel (bayit as temple), pointing ahead to 23:38. Most commentators agree the parable is about 'this evil generation' (12:45); fewer press the temple sense.
- Were Jesus' family against Him? Matthew does not say why they came. Mark 3:21 suggests they thought He was out of His mind; Catholic and Orthodox readers often stress Mary's faithfulness and read 'brothers' as relatives.
- Lilith and the desert creatures Some read Isaiah 34's creatures as ordinary wild animals of a ruin; others, with Heiser, as demonic figures. Ancient translations differ (the Septuagint has 'onocentaurs').

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The video says Ahaz 'responds appropriately' when he will not ask for a sign. Isaiah answers him with a rebuke: 'Is it too slight a thing for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my God as well?' (Isaiah 7:13). Ahaz's pious-sounding refusal hid his unbelief.
- The day of Yahweh text is Isaiah 2:12 (the video says 'Isaiah 6:12').
- Nahum 3 condemns Nineveh's bloodshed and harlotries; its pride is clearest in Zephaniah 2:15: 'I am, and there is no one besides me.'
- Jesus does not refuse to see His mother and brothers in the text; He answers the messenger and points to His disciples.
- The claims credited to Michael Heiser about the wilderness and the desert creatures are summaries we could not check against his books.
- The captions write 'Jonah 1:1 17' for Jonah 1:17, 'liit' for lilith, 'bait' for bayit, and 'BL' for Bethel.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. Have you ever asked God for a sign when He had already shown you enough? What was underneath the request?
2. How are the Pharisees like the Ninevites and the queen of Sheba, and how are they unlike them?
3. What does it mean for a heart to be 'swept and put in order' but empty? How is that dangerous?
4. What fills your 'house' when something bad is cleared out of it?
5. Who are your brothers and sisters by Jesus' definition in 12:50?
6. Where might you be unwilling to recognize God's activity right now?

## Application
- (video) The lesson for the original audience: God is unwilling to reveal His activity to those who are unwilling to recognize it. The scribes and Pharisees refused to recognize Jesus as Lord and Savior, and because of their personal vendetta they blinded themselves to the true explanation for the miracles they saw. This cuts deep, and it is not only for those outside the church. Remember Jesus' prayer: hidden from the wise, revealed to little children (11:25-26). Humility, trust and dependence are the key to God revealing His will. At our salvation we cried out to God in humility, recognizing our sin and our need. That is only the beginning: God's activity does not stop at the point of our salvation, and we are invited to take part in His continuing work. So we must stay in that posture, humble, trusting and dependent on the Lord at all times, so that we keep recognizing His activity all around us.
- Study note (added): read Jonah 3 and 1 Kings 10:1-9 this week. Each evening, write one way you saw God at work that day, and one place you were tempted to demand more proof before obeying.
